title: COLREG lights and shapes — Rules 21-31
source: Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972 (COLREG 72), as amended. Part C, Rules 20-31 (Lights and Shapes) and Annex I (Positioning and technical details of lights and shapes).
disclaimer: Training aid. Wording is summarised, not quoted verbatim; the official IMO publication governs.

conventions.arc: Named arcs resolve against ARCS in js/lights.js: MASTHEAD 225, SIDELIGHT 112.5, STERNLIGHT 135, TOWING 135, ALL_ROUND 360.
conventions.arcCentre: Relative bearing of the arc centre from the bow: MASTHEAD 0, SIDELIGHT_STBD 56.25, SIDELIGHT_PORT 303.75, STERNLIGHT 180, ALL_ROUND 0.
conventions.order: Lights that share a vertical stack are listed highest first, matching how the Rules describe them.

entries.name: Power-driven vessel underway, less than 12 m
entries.summary: May exhibit an all-round white light and sidelights in lieu of the masthead/stern arrangement of Rule 23(a).

lights.label: All-round white
lights.position: Where best seen; may be off the centreline if centreline fitting is impracticable — Rule 23(d)(iii)

quizHints.keySignature: One all-round white plus sidelights — no separate sternlight.

entries.name: Power-driven vessel underway, less than 50 m
entries.summary: One masthead light forward, sidelights and a sternlight. A vessel of less than 50 m is not obliged to carry the second masthead light, but may.

lights.label: Masthead light
lights.position: Forward, not less than 6 m above the hull — Annex I §2(a)(i)

lights.label: Starboard sidelight
lights.position: Starboard side, not above three quarters of the masthead light height — Annex I §2(g)

quizHints.keySignature: A single masthead light: from ahead you see one white light over the sidelights, not two.

entries.name: Power-driven vessel underway, 50 m or more
entries.summary: Two masthead lights — the after one abaft of and higher than the forward one — sidelights and a sternlight. The pair of masthead lights is what gives you her heading and her size.

lights.label: Forward masthead light
lights.position: Forward, not less than 6 m above the hull — Annex I §2(a)(i)

lights.label: After masthead light
lights.position: Abaft of and at least 4.5 m higher than the forward masthead light — Annex I §2(a)(ii)

quizHints.keySignature: Two masthead lights, the after one higher — a 50 m or larger power-driven vessel.

entries.name: Air-cushion vessel in non-displacement mode
entries.summary: The lights of Rule 23(a), plus an all-round flashing yellow light.

quizHints.keySignature: Flashing yellow all-round on an otherwise ordinary power-driven vessel.

entries.name: WIG craft taking off, landing or in flight near the surface
entries.summary: Only when taking off, landing or in flight near the surface: the lights of Rule 23(a) plus a high-intensity all-round flashing red light.

quizHints.keySignature: Flashing RED all-round — WIG craft, not an air-cushion vessel.

entries.name: Power-driven vessel towing, length of tow 200 m or less
entries.summary: Two masthead lights in a vertical line in place of the Rule 23(a)(i)/(ii) light, sidelights, a sternlight, and a yellow towing light in a vertical line above the sternlight.

lights.label: Towing light (yellow)
lights.position: In a vertical line above the sternlight

quizHints.keySignature: Yellow over white from astern — the towing light above the sternlight.

entries.name: Power-driven vessel towing, length of tow exceeding 200 m
entries.summary: As for a shorter tow but with THREE masthead lights in a vertical line, and by day a diamond shape where it can best be seen. The length of tow is measured from the stern of the towing vessel to the after end of the tow.

lights.label: Towing light (yellow)
lights.position: In a vertical line above the sternlight

dayShapes.note: Exhibited by the towing vessel when the tow exceeds 200 m.

quizHints.keySignature: Three masthead lights in a vertical line — the tow is longer than 200 m.

entries.name: Vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside as a composite unit
entries.summary: A pushing vessel and a vessel being pushed ahead that are rigidly connected in a composite unit are regarded as one power-driven vessel and exhibit the lights of Rule 23.

lights.label: After masthead light
lights.position: Abaft of and higher than the forward one

quizHints.keySignature: Indistinguishable from an ordinary power-driven vessel — that is the point of a composite unit.

entries.name: Power-driven vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside (not a composite unit)
entries.summary: Two masthead lights in a vertical line, sidelights and a sternlight. Note there is no yellow towing light — that belongs to a vessel towing astern.

quizHints.keySignature: Two masthead lights in a vertical line but NO yellow towing light.

entries.name: Vessel or object being towed
entries.summary: Sidelights and a sternlight; and, when the length of tow exceeds 200 m, a diamond shape where it can best be seen. No masthead lights.

dayShapes.note: Only when the length of tow exceeds 200 m.

quizHints.keySignature: Sidelights and sternlight with no masthead light at all — she is not propelling herself.

entries.name: Sailing vessel underway
entries.summary: Sidelights and a sternlight. No masthead light — that absence is the whole signature of a sailing vessel at night.

quizHints.keySignature: Sidelights and sternlight, no masthead light.

entries.name: Sailing vessel underway, less than 20 m — combined lantern
entries.summary: In a sailing vessel of less than 20 m the lights of Rule 25(a) may be combined in one lantern carried at or near the top of the mast where it can best be seen.

quizHints.keySignature: All three sectors at one height, high up — a tricolour on a yacht under 20 m.

entries.name: Sailing vessel underway with optional masthead red over green
entries.summary: In addition to the lights of Rule 25(a), two all-round lights in a vertical line at or near the top of the mast — upper red, lower green. These must NOT be exhibited together with the combined lantern of Rule 25(b).

lights.label: All-round red (upper)
lights.position: At or near the top of the mast

lights.label: All-round green (lower)
lights.position: Beneath the red, at or near the top of the mast

quizHints.keySignature: Red over green, sailing machine — the optional masthead pair of Rule 25(c).

entries.name: Vessel under oars
entries.summary: May exhibit the lights prescribed for a sailing vessel; if she does not, she shall have ready at hand an electric torch or lighted lantern showing a white light, exhibited in sufficient time to prevent collision.

lights.label: Torch or lantern (white)
lights.position: Shown in sufficient time to prevent collision

quizHints.keySignature: An intermittent white light with nothing else — the torch of Rule 25(d).

entries.name: Vessel under sail also being propelled by machinery
entries.summary: By day, a conical shape apex downwards, forward where it can best be seen. She is a power-driven vessel for the purposes of Part B and therefore shows the Rule 23 lights at night.

dayShapes.note: Forward, where it can best be seen.

quizHints.keySignature: A cone point-down by day — sails up but engine running, so treat her as power-driven.

entries.name: Vessel engaged in trawling
entries.summary: Two all-round lights in a vertical line, GREEN over WHITE; a masthead light abaft of and higher than the green light (a vessel of less than 50 m is not obliged to carry it); and, when making way, sidelights and a sternlight. By day, two cones apexes together.

lights.label: Masthead light
lights.position: Abaft of and higher than the all-round green light

lights.label: Starboard sidelight
lights.position: Starboard side — only when making way

lights.label: Port sidelight
lights.position: Port side — only when making way

lights.label: Sternlight
lights.position: At the stern — only when making way

dayShapes.note: Two cones with their apexes together in a vertical line.

quizHints.keySignature: GREEN over WHITE — trawling. "Green over white, trawling at night."

entries.name: Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling
entries.summary: Two all-round lights in a vertical line, RED over WHITE; and, when making way, sidelights and a sternlight. By day, two cones apexes together.

lights.label: Starboard sidelight
lights.position: Starboard side — only when making way

lights.label: Port sidelight
lights.position: Port side — only when making way

lights.label: Sternlight
lights.position: At the stern — only when making way

dayShapes.note: Two cones with their apexes together in a vertical line.

quizHints.keySignature: RED over WHITE — fishing, not trawling. "Red over white, fishing at night."

entries.name: Vessel fishing with outlying gear extending more than 150 m
entries.summary: As for fishing other than trawling, plus an all-round white light — or, by day, a cone apex upwards — in the direction of the gear.

lights.label: All-round white — direction of gear
lights.position: In the direction of the outlying gear

dayShapes.note: In the direction of the gear.

quizHints.keySignature: Red over white plus a third white offset to one side — her gear runs that way for over 150 m.

entries.name: Vessel not under command, not making way
entries.summary: Two all-round RED lights in a vertical line where they can best be seen, and by day two balls in a vertical line. No sidelights or sternlight while she is not making way through the water.

quizHints.keySignature: Two all-round reds and nothing else — "red over red, the captain is dead."

entries.name: Vessel not under command, making way
entries.summary: The two all-round red lights, plus sidelights and a sternlight when making way through the water. Still no masthead light — she is not under command.

quizHints.keySignature: Two reds with sidelights but no masthead light — NUC still moving through the water.

entries.name: Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
entries.summary: Three all-round lights in a vertical line — highest and lowest RED, middle WHITE. By day, ball–diamond–ball. Does not apply to a vessel engaged in mine clearance.

quizHints.keySignature: Red–white–red in a vertical line — "restricted man."

entries.name: Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way
entries.summary: The red–white–red group, and in addition masthead light(s), sidelights and a sternlight when making way through the water.

quizHints.keySignature: Red–white–red WITH a masthead light and sidelights — RAM under way and making way.

entries.name: Vessel engaged in a towing operation that severely restricts the tow's ability to deviate
entries.summary: The red–white–red lights and ball–diamond–ball shapes of Rule 27(b), in addition to the full towing display of Rule 24(a).

quizHints.keySignature: A towing display AND red–white–red — she cannot deviate from her course.

entries.name: Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in ability to manoeuvre
entries.summary: The red–white–red group of Rule 27(b), plus two all-round RED lights (or two balls) marking the side on which the obstruction lies, and two all-round GREEN lights (or two diamonds) marking the side on which another vessel may pass.

lights.label: Obstruction side — red (upper)
lights.position: On the side where the obstruction exists

lights.label: Obstruction side — red (lower)
lights.position: On the side where the obstruction exists

lights.label: Safe-pass side — green (upper)
lights.position: On the side on which another vessel may pass

lights.label: Safe-pass side — green (lower)
lights.position: On the side on which another vessel may pass

quizHints.keySignature: Two reds one side, two greens the other — pass on the green side.

entries.name: Vessel engaged in diving operations (small vessel)
entries.summary: Where her size makes the full Rule 27(d) display impracticable: three all-round lights in a vertical line, highest and lowest red and the middle white, and a rigid replica of the International Code flag "A" not less than 1 m in height.

dayShapes.note: Not less than 1 m in height; measures taken to ensure all-round visibility.

quizHints.keySignature: Red–white–red on a small craft with flag A — divers down.

entries.name: Vessel engaged in mine clearance operations
entries.summary: The Rule 23 lights for a power-driven vessel, plus three all-round GREEN lights or three balls — one near the foremast head and one at each end of the fore yard. Other vessels shall not approach within 1000 m.

lights.label: All-round green — starboard yardarm
lights.position: Starboard end of the fore yard

lights.label: All-round green — port yardarm
lights.position: Port end of the fore yard

dayShapes.arrangement: one at the foremast head and one at each end of the fore yard

quizHints.keySignature: Three greens in a triangle — keep 1000 m clear.

entries.name: Vessel constrained by her draught
entries.summary: May exhibit, in addition to the Rule 23 lights, three all-round RED lights in a vertical line, or a cylinder, where they can best be seen.

lights.label: After masthead light
lights.position: Abaft of and higher than the forward one

quizHints.keySignature: Three all-round reds in a vertical line, with normal power-driven lights still showing.

entries.name: Pilot vessel on pilotage duty, underway
entries.summary: Two all-round lights in a vertical line at or near the masthead — upper WHITE, lower RED — and, when underway, sidelights and a sternlight in addition.

quizHints.keySignature: WHITE over RED — "white over red, pilot ahead." Note the order is the reverse of fishing's red over white.

entries.name: Pilot vessel on pilotage duty, at anchor
entries.summary: The white-over-red identity lights, plus the anchor light(s) or shape prescribed by Rule 30.

quizHints.keySignature: White over red plus an anchor light — a pilot boat waiting on station.

entries.name: Vessel at anchor, less than 50 m
entries.summary: May exhibit a single all-round white light where it can best be seen, instead of the two lights of Rule 30(a). By day, one ball in the fore part.

quizHints.keySignature: One all-round white and nothing else, not moving.

entries.name: Vessel at anchor, 50 m or more
entries.summary: An all-round white light in the fore part, and a second all-round white light at or near the stern and LOWER than the forward one. A vessel of 100 m or more shall also use available working lights to illuminate her decks.

lights.label: Anchor light (aft, lower)
lights.position: At or near the stern, lower than the forward light

quizHints.keySignature: Two whites, the forward one HIGHER — a large vessel at anchor. Deck lights are the giveaway at 100 m and over.

entries.name: Vessel aground
entries.summary: The anchor lights of Rule 30(a) or (b), plus two all-round RED lights in a vertical line where they can best be seen. By day, three balls in a vertical line.

quizHints.keySignature: Two reds PLUS anchor lights — aground, not merely not under command. Three balls by day.

entries.name: Seaplane or WIG craft unable to comply
entries.summary: Where it is impracticable for a seaplane or a WIG craft to exhibit lights and shapes of the characteristics or in the positions prescribed by the Rules of Part C, she shall exhibit lights and shapes as closely similar in characteristics and position as is possible.

lights.label: Masthead light (as close as possible)
lights.position: As near the prescribed position as practicable

quizHints.keySignature: Rule 31 is the seaplane exception — it relaxes position and characteristics, not the requirement to show lights.
